text:
jordan: Heads-up — I'm proposing a 'thresholded surgeon' approach for staged rollouts + automatic fallback. want feedback before i write an RFC.

emily: quick tl;dr?

jordan: short version: split canary -> ramp -> steady. each stage has explicit health thresholds (latency P95, error rate, model-quality reg tests). if a threshold trips we run a graded fallback sequence instead of full rollback: 1) traffic shed to safe variant, 2) enable degraded mode (smaller batch/sequence), 3) circuit to older model. the "surgeon" bit is about surgical, minimal-impact interventions rather than blunt swaps.

nikhil: i like surgical idea. how do you decide ordering of interventions? prioritize least-user-visible?

jordan: exactly. ordering by user-impact score + recoverability. example ordering: 1) reduce batch sizes (low impact), 2) restrict new-prefetch cache usage, 3) switch traffic to lower-cost variant, 4) full model rollback. each step has a short cooldown and re-eval window.

lina: do we have metrics hooks for model-quality reg tests in the rollout pipeline? currently those live in the evals job.

jordan: good point — plan is to add a lightweight inline evaler that runs a small probe set (50 prompts) at each stage and reports a quality delta. not full evals; just high-signal checks.

emily: can you share a config sketch? even pseudo-yaml will help ops.

jordan: sure — rough idea:
```yaml
rollout: 
  stages:
    - name: canary
      pct: 1
      wait: 5m
      thresholds:
        latency_p95_ms: 800
        error_rate_pct: 0.5
        qual_drop_pct: 1.5
      fallback_sequence: [reduce_batch, disable_cache, route_to_variant]
    - name: ramp
      pct: 25
      wait: 15m
      thresholds: { ... }
      fallback_sequence: [reduce_batch, route_to_variant, rollback]
    - name: steady
      pct: 100
      thresholds: { ... }
```

nikhil: interesting. where do circuit breakers live? per-route or global?

jordan: per-route by default, with a tenant-global override. reasoning: different customers have different tolerance / SLAs. routing policy supports tenant tags.

lina: what's the signal fusion method? we should avoid flip-flopping on noisy spikes.

jordan: we use a short rolling window + hysteresis. each threshold is evaluated with a 3-sample majority over the window (e.g., 1m, 3m, 5m). and there's an escalation counter: only after N consecutive failures do we take the next fallback step.

emily: can oncall-bot be wired to post the candidate fallback and allow manual abort?

jordan: yes — plan: oncall-bot posts an action card with buttons: [approve step, abort, escalate to owner]. automatic flow waits 30s for manual override before continuing.

oncall-bot: ACTION: rollout 2026-03-21T12:14Z canary triggered fallback_step=reduce_batch. auto-continue in 30s.

ikhil: how do we test the sequence in staging? we need a stager that can inject faults and simulate threshold trips.

jordan: we'll add a 'surgeon mode' test harness that can fake metrics and run through fallback branches. basically a chaos-lite runner that exercises the policy graph.

lina: any thoughts on observability? need clear traces showing which step ran, latency before/after, and customer impact map.

emily: and the console should show a compact timeline and easy rollback button if operators decide to override.

jordan: agreed. minimal UI: stage timeline, current state, last probe results, and quick revert. also expose the policy as JSON so infra can lint and simulate.

ikhil: what about multi-variant experiments (A/B) where you want partial rollbacks per variant?

jordan: policy supports variant-scoped sequences. fallback can be targeted to a variant or to the whole traffic set. default to targeted.

lina: one risk: cascading fallbacks causing capacity spike on fallback variant. we need capacity-aware ordering.

jordan: good catch — add a capacity check step before routing more traffic to a variant. if capacity insufficient, pick alternative fallback (disable cache first) or throttle total routed traffic.

emily: sounds solid. next steps?

jordan: i'll draft an RFC with: state machine diagram, policy DSL, tests (surgeon-mode harness), and console wireframes. will ping reviewers.

ikhil: +1 — please include failure cases and example postmortem template.

lina: +1, and include per-tenant SLA knobs.

emily: also include an annex: how this interacts with canary mirroring vs live routing.

jordan: thanks — will send RFC tomorrow.

emily: :thumbsup: 

lina: :100: 

ikhil: thanks!
